tagline: A mile and a half of gravel, kept the old way.
intro: McAuley Road runs 1.6 miles from Huntersville-Concord Road to NC 73, unpaved the whole way, in a county the state's guidebook counts among the fastest-growing urban areas in the United States. Five minutes of driving, if nobody stops.

The Charlotte Mecklenburg Historic Landmarks Commission calls it one of the last vestiges of the rural vistas that held the county until the middle of the 20th century, and the Catawba Lands Conservancy keeps 775 acres around it under conservation easements.

moments.title: Rolling farm country
moments.text: Rolling hills, mixed woods, pasture with grazing livestock and old farm buildings line the dirt road in what the guidebook calls a typical 19th-century landscape.

moments.title: Ramah Creek bridge
moments.text: About halfway along, a one-lane wooden bridge crosses Ramah Creek, which meanders through the protected land on either side.

practical: The road is gravel for its whole length and crosses Ramah Creek on a one-lane wooden bridge.
